items.title: Python's F-String for String Interpolation and Formatting
items.description: Python f-strings give you a readable, concise way to interpolate and format strings, and they beat .format() and the % operator on speed.
items.summary: Python f-strings offer a concise and efficient way to interpolate variables, objects , and expressions directly into strings. By prefixing a string with f or F , you can embed expressions within curly braces ( {} ), which are evaluated at runtime .

items.title: Get Started With Django: Build a Portfolio App

items.title: Python's property(): Add Managed Attributes to Your Classes
items.description: Use Python's property() to add managed attributes to your classes, with validation, computed values, and caching, without breaking your API.
items.summary: The @property decorator simplifies the management of attributes in your Python classes . It allows you to control attribute access, enabling features such as data validation, lazy evaluation , and the creation of backward-compatible APIs without modifying the class’s public interface.

items.title: NumPy Tutorial: Your First Steps Into Data Science in Python
items.description: Follow this NumPy tutorial to learn how to create and manipulate arrays in Python and take your first steps into data science.
items.summary: NumPy is a Python library that provides a simple yet powerful data structure : the n-dimensional array . This is the foundation on which almost all the power of Python’s data science toolkit is built, and learning NumPy is the first step on any Python data scientist’s journey.

items.title: Python Metaclasses
items.description: How Python's metaclasses work as an OOP concept, what they are good for—and why you might want to avoid them in your own programs.
items.summary: The term metaprogramming refers to the potential for a program to have knowledge of or manipulate itself. Python supports a form of metaprogramming for classes called metaclasses .

items.title: What Is the Python Global Interpreter Lock (GIL)?
items.description: The Python GIL is a mutex that lets only one thread control the interpreter at a time. Learn how it shapes your program's performance.
items.summary: The Python Global Interpreter Lock or GIL , in simple words, is a mutex (or a lock) that allows only one thread to hold the control of the Python interpreter. This means that only one thread can be in a state of execution at any point in time.

items.title: Operators and Expressions in Python
items.description: Python operators are the symbols and keywords that build expressions. Learn how to combine them with objects to compute real results.
items.summary: Python operators enable you to perform computations by combining objects and operators into expressions. Understanding Python operators is essential for manipulating data effectively.

items.title: Python Plotting With Matplotlib (Guide)
items.description: This article is a beginner-to-intermediate-level walkthrough on Python and matplotlib that mixes theory with example.
items.summary: A picture is worth a thousand words, and with Python’s matplotlib library, it fortunately takes far less than a thousand words of code to create a production-quality graphic. However, matplotlib is also a massive library, and getting a plot to look just right is often achieved through trial and error.

items.title: Speed Up Your Python Program With Concurrency
items.description: Explore Python concurrency with threading, asyncio, and multiprocessing, and learn which model speeds up your I/O-bound or CPU-bound programs.
items.summary: Concurrency refers to the ability of a program to manage multiple tasks at once, improving performance and responsiveness. It encompasses different models like threading, asynchronous tasks, and multiprocessing, each offering unique benefits and trade-offs.

items.title: Python and REST APIs: Interacting With Web Services
items.description: Learn to consume web services with the requests library, then explore the tools for building a Python REST API of your own.
items.summary: There’s an amazing amount of data available on the Web. Many web services , like YouTube and GitHub, make their data accessible to third-party applications through an application programming interface (API) .

items.title: Supply Chain Security for the Age of AI-Speed Exploits
items.description: Learn Python supply chain security as AI speeds up attacks: what the LiteLLM backdoor teaches, how to check your setup, and habits that last.
items.summary: Python supply chain security means protecting everything your project pulls in and runs, from PyPI packages to CI workflows and publishing credentials, so that a tampered release or stolen token can’t turn your own tools against you. AI-assisted analysis makes it cheaper to turn a bug fix into a working exploit, so attacks now arrive within hours of a fix, and sometimes before it.
